claims.text: The formation and persistence of a protective oxide on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C is governed by the selective oxidation kinetics of X.
Si additions promote a continuous, adherent silica-containing oxide through surface enrichment and diffusion.
Al additions promote a continuous, adherent alumina-containing oxide through surface enrichment and diffusion.
Mn-containing variants form unstable scales because of Mn-oxide volatility and mismatched oxide growth.
High-temperature exposure causes localized surface enrichment and diffusion of Si or Al at the alloy/scale interface.
Selective oxidation of Cr together with Si or Al forms a dense, continuous silica- or alumina-containing layer.
The silica- or alumina-containing layer adheres strongly to the alloy substrate.
Mn-rich oxides are less stable because of greater volatility or oxide/alloy volume mismatch.
Instability of Mn-rich oxides results in scale cracking or spallation.
Differences in oxide-formation thermodynamics, oxidation kinetics, and strain accommodation determine scale adhesion.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, Si- and Al-containing alloys will maintain coherent protective scales, whereas Mn-containing alloys will crack or spall.
Si- and Al-modified alloys will have significantly greater oxidation resistance than CrFeCoNi without X.
CrFeCoNi without X is proposed as a baseline, with the alternative of directly comparing variants differing only in X.
The proposed behavior applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states under oxidative or corrosive exposure at or above approximately 900 °C over extended periods.
Comparable cracking, spallation, or non-adherent morphology in the Si/Al and Mn variants would falsify the proposed selective-oxidation mechanism.
Similar oxide behavior for all alloy variants regardless of X would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The temperature boundary alternates between strictly above 900 °C and greater than or equal to 900 °C, leaving applicability at exactly 900 °C inconsistent.
